title: Ghost traffic amplification during regional failover — investigation & remediation plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 at ~22:14 UTC we observed a multi-region event where traffic intended for a degraded primary region amplified ('ghost traffic') against the secondary region due to synchronous failover coordination between edge routing and internal client libraries. The amplification caused transient queueing and p99 latency SLO violations for ~47 minutes and triggered emergency throttles, degrading throughput for multiple customers.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-09 22:12 UTC: A regional networking flake increased tail latency in region-us-west-2 causing elevated error rates for several availability zones.

2026-03-09 22:14 UTC: Control plane initiated failover for affected host groups. Edge routers and client library health check detectors both began failover procedures with no jitter, causing a synchronized traffic shift.

2026-03-09 22:15 UTC: Circuit breakers in the secondary region tripped due to sudden fan-in; hysteresis values routed traffic back, which triggered immediate retries from clients; retries plus new failover traffic produced a >3x instantaneous request rate spike.
2026-03-09 22:20 UTC: Tokenized request queues in the secondary region exceeded soft queue thresholds; KV cache cold-start led to additional compute per request and increased per-token latency.
2026-03-09 22:40 UTC: SRE team applied emergency throttle rules and manually extended circuit breaker backoff windows; traffic stabilized by 23:01 UTC.
2026-03-09 23:01 UTC: All automated protections returned to normal. Post-incident monitoring remained active for 24 hours.

Observed impact: p99 latency breached 99.9% target for 47 minutes; sustained tail latency increase of ~200ms at p95; error rates for some customers rose to 2.4% (baseline 0.1%); peak failover-induced request amplification measured ~3.6x above steady-state ingress.
Customers: Impact visible to hosted API customers in NA with multi-region routing and to a small set of Dedicated customers with cross-region replication enabled.
root_causes: 1) Failover synchronization: edge router failover and internal client-library health check triggered nearly simultaneously with no randomized jitter, producing a coordinated fanout.

2) Circuit-breaker hysteresis misconfiguration: backoff windows and trip thresholds were tuned for single-source surges, not multi-source synchronized surges; breakers oscillated instead of containing load.
3) KV cache cold-start amplification: cache warming sequence was single-threaded and synchronous, increasing per-request compute and exacerbating latency under surge.

4) Observability blind spot: no metric surfaced immediate retried-request fanout from client libraries during failover; dashboards showed increased ingress but not origin (retry vs new traffic) attribution.
5) Playbook gap: runbook assumed staggered failover by control plane; it did not account for simultaneous client-library failovers at scale.
mitigations_applied_during_incident: Temporarily raised soft queue thresholds in secondary region to avoid immediate shedding while SRE applied targeted throttles.
Manually extended circuit breaker backoff windows and increased sampling to reduce oscillation.
Applied emergency ingress rate limits for non-critical API routes to prioritize latency-sensitive traffic.
Triggered manual cache pre-warm for high-QPS model shards in the secondary region.
Opened a high-priority incident bridge and notified affected customers and account teams.
action_items: ENG-A1: Implement randomized jitter (0-250ms) in client-library failover path and edge router failover to avoid synchronized fanout — owner: Miguel Thompson — due: 2026-03-20
ENG-A2: Revise circuit breaker configuration to include surge-aware hysteresis profiles and per-region decay timers; create automated config rollout with canary — owner: Priya Rao — due: 2026-03-24
ENG-A3: Parallelize KV cache warmup and add background proactive shard warming for promoted regions; add warmup health check signal to placement — owner: Wei Zhang — due: 2026-03-31

ENG-A4: Add telemetry: instrument retry-origin tagging (client-retry vs control-plane-redirect) and a 'failover-fanout' metric; add alert for >2x expected retry ratio — owner: Observability Team (Liam O'Connor) — due: 2026-03-18

ENG-A5: Update failover runbook to include coordinated steps for control plane, edge, and client-library teams and define a staged failover flow with verification gates — owner: SRE (Hannah Kim) — due: 2026-03-22

ENG-A6: Build automated canary for cross-region failover that simulates degraded primary and verifies no >1.5x amplification in secondary under controlled load — owner: Reliability Platform (Julian Park) — due: 2026-04-05
ENG-A7: Create a post-deployment checklist for circuit-breaker tuning changes with latency regressions gated by synthetic traffic — owner: Platform Stability (Sara Mitchell) — due: 2026-03-28
ENG-A8: Customer remediation: outreach email + dedicated post-incident report for affected accounts with credits where appropriate — owner: Customer Success (R. Alvarez) — due: 2026-03-15
follow_up_meetings: 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC: Incident debrief with SRE, Edge, Client SDK, and Observability — outcome: agreed on jitter + telemetry priority
2026-03-18 09:00 UTC: Design review for circuit-breaker surge profiles with Platform Stability and Runtime teams
2026-03-25 14:00 UTC: Failover canary design sign-off and rollout schedule
risks_and_open_questions: Will adding jitter to client libraries interact poorly with some low-latency customers using pinned routing? Need compatibility test matrix.
How to balance faster warmup (more background resources) with cost targets for Dedicated customers? Find performance/cost sweet spot.
Is there any scenario where staggered failover could lengthen outage for a single customer? Document trade-offs in runbook.
notes_and_discussion: 2026-03-10: Asha P. — Initial triage suggests synchronized actions across layers; collecting router logs and client SDK telemetry for correlation.
2026-03-11: Miguel T. — We reproduced coordinated failover in staging when disabling jitter; amplification factor matches production within 10%.
2026-03-11: Hannah K. — SRE will add a temporary alert for retry-origin ratio to catch recurrence while permanent metrics are implemented.
2026-03-12: Priya R. — Draft of new hysteresis config proposed; will run offline worst-case simulations before rollout.
